items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I had a ball. And I was with a Lincoln Center drummer who works with Wynton and everybody.

ctx.x: What do those gigs pay, or do they?

Well I don’t really do any gigs under a hundred bucks. And there are a lot of hundred buck gigs and they have stayed a hundred bucks for a very long time. You know what I mean? So the pay hasn’t gone up in New York in a very long time. You could go as low as, my goodness, my sister did a gig there for like fifteen bucks. I’m like that’s one drink and a tip in New York these days. She makes money in other ways. She’s one of the best copyists there is. You know what I mean? Like she does other gigs that actually do…

night.” That’s the most fun I’ve had on a gig in ages, you know what I mean? So for me it was a hundred bucks but it wasn’t about the hundred bucks. You know club owners know this too, that we want to play music, and often take advantage of us. I just have a bit of a problem with some of the kids coming out of the colleges and playing for twenty, thirty bucks and fifty bucks even. It’s really just not helping to standardize anything. So playing for nothing is not a great idea generally.
